title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment, Reference Architectures, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback, Customer Requirements
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Canonical guide and reference for Redwood Private deployments covering VPC and on-prem deployment steps, recommended reference architectures, on-prem packaging checklist, day-2 operational runbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures. Includes a customer requirements library to accelerate scoping and SOW preparation.
introduction: Purpose: This document centralizes the deployment and operations guidance used by Solutions Engineering, Professional Services, and the Private Deployments team. It is prescriptive: follow the steps and checklists in order and retain the preflight results as part of the customer ticket. Target audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers at customers, DevOps/Cloud Ops, and internal support teams.
architecture_overview: High-level patterns: We support two private deployment modes: 1) VPC-hosted private control plane with customer-managed compute and networking (recommended for cloud-first customers). 2) On-prem appliance style packages for air-gapped or regulated environments. Both modes share the same runtime components (inference runtime, control plane, observability agents) but differ in networking, identity, and data egress constraints. Key components: control plane (optional hosted), model serving runtime (GPU nodes), KV/cache stores, object storage for artifacts, metrics/tracing pipelines, and KMS/HSM integrations.
reference_architectures:
We provide three validated reference architectures depending on customer constraints. 1) Cloud VPC (recommended): control plane hosted by Redwood, data plane in customer VPC. 2) Hybrid (semi-managed): control plane in customer-managed account with optional Redwood assist. 3) On-prem (air-gapped): full stack packaged as OCI images + offline package. Each reference architecture includes network diagrams, required subnets, firewall rules, and minimum capacity profiles. Example minimum capacity table (example for inference-only cluster):

| Role | Min nodes | VM size / GPU | Storage | Notes |
|------|----------:|---------------|--------|-------|
| Control-plane (K8s control plane components) | 3 | 4 vCPU, 16Gi | 100Gi | HA etcd recommended |
| Inference node | 2 | 1xA100(40GB) or 4xT4 | 500Gi NVMe | Scale based on QPS |
| KV cache / redis | 2 | 2 vCPU, 8Gi | 50Gi | replication enabled |

For strict-regulatory customers, use the On-Prem reference and follow the packaging checklist below.
networking_requirements:
Networking and firewall rules (VPC mode):
- Required outbound: control-plane endpoints (TLS 443) to Redwood control-plane CIDRs (documented per-account).
- Required inbound: SSH only from approved admin jump boxes; API endpoints are private and accessible via VPC peering or PrivateLink.
- CIDR allocation guidelines: allocate spare /24 for control-plane services, separate subnets: public (bastion), private (control plane), compute (inference GPUs), storage (object store).
- NAT and Egress: for customers that restrict egress, we support egress proxying through approved IPs; ensure KMS/HSM endpoints are reachable if using cloud KMS.

Checklist (yes/no):
- VPC peering or PrivateLink configured
- Security groups limited to required ports
- Route tables in place
- DNS (private zone) configured for internal service names
onprem_packaging_and_installation:
On-prem packaging model: We deliver an offline bundle that contains signed OCI images, Helm charts, and an installation artifact (tar.gz) with manifest and checksums. Packaging checklist:
- Bundle signed with customer PGP key or Redwood signing (per contract)
- SHA256 checksums and signature file included
- Installation script (install.sh) with idempotent semantics
- Dependencies: container runtime (containerd >=1.7), Kubernetes distribution supported (RKE2, k3s, or customer-provided K8s v1.24+), required kernel modules for GPU drivers, NVIDIA driver matching runtime.

Installation quickstart (high level):
1) Preflight: run ./preflight-check.sh and capture report.
2) Install CRs and namespaces: helm install redwood-core ./charts/redwood-core --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace
3) Apply network policies and node selectors for GPU workloads.
4) Deploy runtime with customer model artifacts pinned via object store URI.

Post-install verification: provide kubeconfigs and run the acceptance tests (./tests/acceptance/run.sh) to validate end-to-end inference path and metrics collection.
preflight_and_prerequisites:
Required before deployment:
- Approved SOW and security questionnaire completed.
- Admin SSH access to management jump host.
- K8s cluster with the minimum node sizes and GPU drivers installed.
- Object store bucket and credentials (S3-compatible or on-prem object store) for model artifacts.
- KMS/HSM details if using customer-managed keys.
- Monitoring endpoints and log forwarding destinations for Prometheus/Alertmanager.

Run the preflight tool and include results in the ticket. Preflight will check: network reachability, disk IO, GPU driver compatibility, required ports, Kubernetes version, and node taints/labels.
vpc_deployment_steps:
VPC Deployment Procedure (recommended for cloud):
1) Kickoff and scoping: confirm region, instance types, and SLOs. 2) Create networking: allocate subnets, configure PrivateLink or VPC peering with Redwood control-plane if applicable. 3) Provision K8s cluster or managed EKS/GKE/AKS cluster following our sizing guidelines. 4) Run preflight tool and resolve any failures. 5) Apply Helm charts with values.yaml prepopulated (example values included below). 6) Configure object store and copy model artifacts. 7) Configure KMS integration and secrets (use sealed-secrets or external secret operator). 8) Run smoke tests and workload simulations. 9) Ramp traffic using staged rollout policy (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%). 10) Hand over runbook and monitoring dashboards.

Example values snippet (values.yaml excerpt):
- replicaCount: 3
- resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "2000m"
      memory: "8Gi"
- gpu:
    enabled: true
    driverVersion: "535.104"
day2_ops_and_runbooks:
Day-2 operations guidance: This section is the canonical runbook set for oncall and customer SREs. It covers scaling, incidentplaybooks, backups, and routine maintenance.

Key SLOs and thresholds:
- API latency (p50/p95/p99) target: 30ms / 120ms / 250ms for text-generation median prompt of 32 tokens.
- Availability SLO: 99.9% for Dedicated/private data-plane (monthly).
- Error budget burn rate alert if >50% of errors are 5xx over a 1-hour window.

Operational runbooks (summary):
1) High CPU/GPU utilization: identify runaway jobs, throttle batcher, apply node autoscaler policies.
2) Spike in latency: check KV cache hit rate, model warm status, and batcher queue depth. 3) Object store errors: validate credentials, check network ACLs, and verify bucket policy. 4) Control plane unreachable: check PrivateLink status, VPN/IPSec tunnels, and firewall rules.

Maintenance tasks (monthly/quarterly):
- Rotate TLS certificates and secrets.
- Run disaster recovery drill for model artifact restoration.
- Validate KMS key rotations and rewrap tokens.

Monitoring & alerts (recommended):
- Prometheus job: redwood-inference-exporter with scrape interval 15s
- Alertmanager rules: HighLatency, LowCacheHitRate, PodOOM, NodeGPUHealth.
- Dashboard: per-route latency, per-model token cost, and token throughput.

Escalation path:
1) Oncall engineer (customer or Redwood)
2) Private Deployments SME (Slack #private-deployments)
3) Eng-SRE pager escalation if infra-level issue
upgrade_and_rollback_procedure:
Upgrade and rollback workflow (applies to both VPC and on-prem):
Pre-upgrade checklist: backup Helm release values, snapshot PVs (if stateful), snapshot object store metadata, ensure canary traffic policy is configured, and run acceptance tests.

Upgrade steps (recommended staged rollout):
1) Create release artifact and tag.
2) Deploy to staging and run full acceptance suite.
3) Schedule maintenance window with customer if required.
4) Deploy canary (single replica per zone or 5% traffic). Monitor for errors for 30-60 minutes.
5) Ramp to 25% then 100% following successful checks.

Rollback immediate steps (on severe regression):
1) Abort rollout and redirect traffic to previous release (or scale previous deployment up).
2) If state schema changed, run rollback migration scripts as documented in release notes.
3) Open incident with root cause hypothesis, collect logs (kube, app, ingress), and retain all artifacts.

Post-incident: perform a rollback postmortem and update the canary checks to catch the regression earlier.
customer_requirements_library:
Customer requirements library (use when scoping pre-sales or SOW). Use the table below to capture expectations and check items during discovery.

| Area | Customer Requirement | Redwood validated option | Notes |
|------|----------------------|--------------------------|-------|
| Networking | PrivateLink / VPC peering | PrivateLink preferred for minimal route table changes | Provide list of Redwood IPs |
| Identity & Access | SAML SSO, RBAC integration | SAML + mapped LDAP groups | Provide IdP metadata |
| Storage | S3-compatible object store | Min 500GB for model artifacts (varies) | Provide endpoint and creds |
| KMS | Customer-managed keys (cloud KMS/HSM) | Supported: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault | Provide key ARN and access policy |
| Compliance | Audit logging retention 1 year | Redwood agent + customer SIEM | Provide SIEM endpoint and format |
| Capacity | Expected QPS and concurrency | We'll map to GPU profile | Provide traffic profile and token distribution |

Discovery checklist (fill during scoping):
- Account IDs and contact persons
- Target regions and availability zones
- SLO targets and peak QPS
- Compliance constraints and required evidence
security_and_compliance_notes:
Security guardrails:
- Default to least privilege for secrets and service accounts.
- All control-plane traffic must use mTLS and be logged.
- Audit logs must be forwarded to customer SIEM in JSON format; retention policy configurable.
- For restricted customers, on-prem deployments require physical access control and FIPS-compliant crypto modules where specified.

Evidence artifacts delivered post-deploy: preflight report, installation manifest, Helm values, Prometheus rules, and acceptance test report.
ownership_and_support:
Ownership: Private Deployments team owns packaging, deployment automation, and runbook maintenance. Eng-SRE owns monitoring, alerting templates, and escalation procedures. Solutions Engineering owns pre-sales scoping and SOW validation.

Support SLA: Tiered: 1) Self-serve docs & runbooks, 2) Professional Services for installs, 3) Enterprise support for on-call and incident response (per contract). Contact: #private-deployments (Slack) and private-deployments@redwood.ai
appendix_and_templates: Included templates: values.yaml example, preflight output sample, acceptance-test checklist, and canary-validation checklist. Example canary validation checks: 200 OK rate > 99%, p95 within 2x baseline, no new 5xx errors, cache hit rate >= 70%.
